I have tried not looking at my phone before going to bed etc. but that does not seem to help with falling asleep. I get anywhere from 6-9 hours of sleep a night.

About a month ago when I went to my GP's office the PA there thought I needed Zoloft "to take the edge off" and potentially anxiety was not letting me rest..  I will add that there are two things that seem to help.The first is if I close my eyes and try to rest as if I am falling sleep. The second one I noticed is exercise. I try to do spin class 2-3 times per week. I noticed after spin class that during the class when I was pushing myself there was no headaches at all. I assume the headaches and lack of sleep are related? How do I get to sleep better and stay rested? Anything else I may be mssing?

Age 43

Sex F

Height 5'2"

Weight 202

Race Caucasian 

Duration of complaint 2ish years 

Location Washington state 

Any existing relevant medical issues: RA, Chiari malformation, Diabetes type 2 (electric boogaloo), sleep apnea, fibromyalgia, ibs, Gerd, hypertension, hyoeelipidemia, hypothyroidism 

Current medications: metformin, Ozempic, Olumiant, atorvastatin, metoprolol, amlodipine, Flonase, zyrtec, omeprazole, vitamins c, e, & b, multivitamin, calcium, magnesium. Also recently using 5mg each thc and cbd nightly.

Social: father passed, husband on dialysis 

Also: recent unexplained high blood sugars, ~180 (have an endocrinologist appt next week)

I've lost and kept off 40 pounds over the last six years, and stopped being insulin dependent. My weight has plateaued the last year.

About 2 years ago I was told I had fatty liver. I continued the diet and exercise I was already doing (the reason for the weight loss) and maybe six months or so later I was told my liver had improved. 

This fall my routine labs from my rheumatologist showed elevated liver enzymes. Two repeat labs showed the same. I was sent to my PCP, who ordered a liver ultrasound.

While I was waiting for ultrasound result, I asked my primary doctor for a referral to a gastroenterologist because I'd been having upper abdominal pain, early satiety, and I hadn't seen a gastro for my Gerd in a while.

Ultrasound results came back. It says stage 1 NASH, no cirrhosis or fibrosis. I Google. Results are conflicting, some are scary. There are multiple terms for this condition, and different sources give different explanations of what the various terms mean. Not clear at all.

I follow up with my PCP. He says it's not actually scary, it's all reversible through diet and exercise. Do that, take vitamin e, no booze. I said I'd read there is medication I could take. He tells me to lose 12 pounds and come back in 3 months. I say I will, but could I also try medication while I'm doing all that? He says no. I feel like he thinks that if he gives me meds I won't do the diet and exercise. I feel this is an unfair assessment because I have a documented ability to lose weight through diet and exercise.

I leave and I plan to do the diet exercise and vitamin e, but I do want to also try a medication I read about. I decide to ask the gastro for it instead.

At gastro appt, he says the same thing as the PCP. It's reversible long term with diet and exercise. He's actually more worried about the abdominal pain and early satiety. He orders blood tests, upper endoscopy, colonoscopy, and pelvic CT.

I say I'm on board with the tests, diet, and exercise, but could I also try a medication. He says yes, he wants me to take a medication. I ask what it is and he says it's actually an otc suppliment. His nurse will come in and tell me more about it. It's very effective, and the nurse's husband happens to take it. Um, ok?

Doc leaves, nurse comes in. The suppliment is called Advaclear. She tells me I can buy it on Amazon or from the manufacturer website. No referral code.

So I'm feeling weird about this. My PCP didn't tell me to take a specific brand of vitamin e, he just told me to take 300 iu of vitamin e. I Google this suppliment and it's described as a detox. Red flag, lots of quack medicine talks about detox. There's lots of websites and product reviews claiming this thing works, but of course there are. That's true of any suppliment.

I used to be big into suppliments. My ex worked for a suppliment retailer. But, long story short, I learned about how they're not regulated and most of the things they're supposed to do are unverified. Also very alarming how there's basically no tracking for drug interactions involving suppliments. I have multiple medical conditions and take multiple prescriptions, so I am very leery about adding more pills into the mix.

Does anyone have any info about Advaclear? Does it work? Is this a red flag? Should I get a second opinion? Should I go back and ask more questions about the suppliment? Should I just proceed with diet, exercise, vitamin e, and testing and revisit the suppliment issue at my next appt? Is this a common treatment for this condition that actually works? As far as I can tell the doctor and nurse aren't getting any kind of kickback or profit from referring me.

Hello, everyone! I brought this up to my PCP who first suggested I try various OTC laxatives (which didn’t really do much), then later referred me to a gastroenterologist who recommended fiber and put me on lactulose, which I tried for around a few months which either did nothing or a couple times gave me uncontrollable explosive diarrhea with no therapeutic range where I could just have a normal bowel movement. I finally got the GI doc to give me a colonoscopy which came back normal, so he told me to just continue with the fiber and laxatives which were already not helping, so I basically just gave up on getting professional help for a while.  
  
I’m now almost 35 and trying to take my health more seriously, and as a registered nurse I know that what I’m experiencing is not normal and needs further evaluation. I go on bouts (I know I should be more consistent but struggle due to the untreated ADHD, also on the waitlist for a behavioral health provider) of taking fiber, magnesium citrate, and pre-/pro-biotics which are helping some, and I’m basically to the point where I can sometimes initiate a BM naturally (especially if I wait longer than usual/comfortable once I’ve had the sensation that I need to go) but still not go completely without digital stool removal or using an enema for the rest.  
  
Other relevant information:  
\-My stool is usually medium-brown in color, soft-formed or mushy, rarely hard/pebbly, I often express clear mucus from my rectum with or without stool, occasionally thick whitish stringy material in stool itself, and I’ve noticed that some of the time when I have a BM without assistance it is very narrow (around finger-width) and sort of flat as if my internal anal sphincter doesn’t like to fully/easily open (often feels like this when I insert fingers as well).  
\-I often have BLQ abdominal tenderness to palpation.  
\-I do get rare shooting pain from my anus to my penis; only happened a handful of times or so and seems random/unrelated to bowel movements or assisted stool removal.  
\-I have a small nodule (maybe pen-tip size if that) in my posterior rectum about 1 inch in (appeared \~1.5 years ago, is small, soft, and has not grown in size; assessed by a family practice doc who gave me a referral to infectious disease despite all my STI tests coming back negative, that office said I should get a referral to a colo-rectal specialist, so I told the ordering doc and he just never got back to me). I assume it’s from all the mild trauma initiated by digital insertion, enemas, and occasional anal sexual activity (see below) but don’t know for sure.  
\-I do “bottom” and use anal sex toys a few times a year and have done so since my early teens, but I frequently avoid such activities due to my GI issues.  
  
Sorry for the long-winded post, but I have a physical w/ my PCP next month and hope to have some suggestions of what to explore/tell her and maybe some advice of what I can do on my own to help. This has been a major and shameful struggle in my life for well over a decade now, and I just want it to go away. Thank you in advance!
